$comment: Ported from the Compound Labs copy gates. Each pattern carries scope flags: copy (outward copy, which is what NewsRail checks), answer and reply. A pattern may carry requires, unless (regexes tested against the sentence around the hit) and min_words.
rule: Information, not prose. Before each sentence, ask who reads it and what they need from it. One fact per sentence: subject, verb, object.
copy_rule: Information, not prose. Copy says what the subject does and what the reader gets, in plain sentences with a subject and a verb. No metaphor for the product, no caption in front of a link, no money figure without saying who pays, and no label alone on a line in place of a sentence.

1.name: caption-for-a-link
1.title: CAPTION FOR A LINK
1.what: a noun phrase ending in a colon in front of a link, in place of a sentence that says what the link is

2.name: figure-without-payer
2.title: FIGURE WITHOUT A PAYER
2.what: a percent or dollar figure about money with no clause saying who pays or gets it

3.name: product-metaphor
3.title: METAPHOR FOR THE PRODUCT
3.what: a metaphor or coined name standing in for the product or its output in outward copy

4.name: label-not-sentence
4.title: LABEL IN PLACE OF A SENTENCE
4.what: a noun phrase ending in a colon alone on a line, followed by prose or a link instead of a list

5.name: modifier-tail
5.title: MODIFIER TAIL ON A NAME
5.what: a naming fragment (a tagline, theme, headline or card line) with a relative clause or a participial phrase hung off the noun instead of just saying the plain noun

patterns.fix: write a sentence that says what the link is: Here is a demo video: <link>
put the figure in a clause with a payer and a verb: You pay 25 percent of what the state grants.
use the product's own site words: demo video, statements, protests, the product name
write the sentence the label stands for: Here is a demo video: <link>, or The state deadline is thirty days.
say the plain noun and stop: "four ranking sites", not "four boards, recounted every night"
say the plain noun and stop: "four ranking sites", not "four rankings nobody can buy their way onto"
